style_bible.lighting: single-source chiaroscuro, hard stairwell light, practical pools, visible darkness

scenes.narration: Elias's newspaper was dated tomorrow. He lived alone. He had no subscription.
scenes.visual: Predawn apartment corridor. A folded broadsheet lies square on a worn doormat, edges damp. No footsteps, no shadow under any door.
characters: Elias Voss - 34, gaunt, dark wool coat, close-cropped hair, sleepless
scenes.environment: Narrow 1970s apartment corridor, mustard wallpaper, one flickering stairwell light
scenes.lighting: Hard sodium light from the stairwell; the doormat is the brightest object in frame
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic vertical 9:16 still, 1970s apartment corridor at 4:50 a.m., a folded broadsheet newspaper on a worn doormat, mustard wallpaper, one hard sodium stairwell light, deep teal shadows, visible dust, 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine 16mm grain, no legible text, no people

scenes.narration: A misprint — until page nine reported his death. Apartment fire. Friday. Three a.m. His name.
scenes.visual: Macro on page nine. A fingertip stops under a short column circled faintly in red pencil. The newsprint is dense and unreadable except for the date at the top.
characters: Elias Voss - hand and forearm only, ink stain on the thumb
scenes.environment: Kitchen table, cold coffee ring, ashtray, overhead bulb
scenes.lighting: Single bare bulb three feet above the page; hard falloff at the frame edges
scenes.camera: Macro push in from 50mm, slight handheld drift
scenes.image_prompt: Extreme close-up, vertical 9:16, aged newsprint on a kitchen table lit by one bare bulb, a forefinger resting under a circled column, dense illegible print texture, red pencil mark, cold coffee ring, hard shadows, 50mm macro, shallow focus, fine 16mm grain, no readable words

scenes.narration: He booked a hotel across town. Saturday's paper was at the front desk.
scenes.visual: Cheap hotel room. Elias kneels to unplug a lamp, then the television. A digital clock reads 3:00. Through the window, the city glows without detail.
characters: Elias Voss - 34, coat still on, movements too deliberate
scenes.environment: Budget hotel room, patterned carpet, heavy curtains, laminated headboard
scenes.lighting: Lamp light on the floor, blue window spill, clock digits red
scenes.camera: Locked-off wide, then slow tilt down to the clock
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic vertical 9:16 still, budget hotel room at night, a man in a dark coat kneeling to unplug a lamp, patterned carpet, heavy curtains, red digital clock reading 3:00, blue window light, teal shadows, 35mm lens, fine 16mm grain, tense stillness, no text besides the clock

scenes.narration: The fire happened anyway. Same building. Same hour. Different man. The dead man was his neighbour, who'd knocked to warn him.
scenes.visual: Hotel front desk at dawn. A newspaper waits beside a brass bell. Dissolve to the neighbour's door: three knocks, a tray of biscuits left untouched, police tape reflected in the brass.
scenes.environment: Hotel lobby with moth-eaten carpet; later the same corridor as scene 1, now sealed
scenes.lighting: Dawn through frosted glass, one desk lamp; corridor lit by a single emergency bulb
scenes.camera: Slow dolly across the desk, dissolve to a locked-off corridor shot
scenes.image_prompt: Cinematic vertical 9:16 still, hotel reception desk at dawn, folded newspaper beside a brass bell, clerk half out of frame, frosted glass light, teal and amber, 35mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine 16mm grain, quiet menace, no legible text, no watermark

scenes.narration: Elias spread every paper he'd saved across the floor. All dated tomorrow. Each mentioned him less than the last.
scenes.visual: Top-down. Dozens of newspapers tile the floor like a grid. Elias kneels at the centre, comparing two front pages. A lamp casts a hard circle over him.
characters: Elias Voss - 34, sleeves rolled, hands ink-stained
scenes.environment: His apartment floor, bare boards, radiator, one lamp with no shade
scenes.lighting: Single lamp pool from the left; the rest of the room sinks into black
scenes.image_prompt: Overhead vertical 9:16 still, dozens of newspapers arranged in a grid across bare wooden floorboards, a kneeling man in shirtsleeves at the centre, one hard lamp pool, deep black edges, teal shadows, 35mm lens, fine 16mm grain, obsessive symmetry, no readable text

scenes.narration: First his job. Then his friends. Then the crossword. By Friday, his photograph was a grey rectangle.
scenes.visual: Close on a crossword with three names erased into grey blocks. Beside it, a framed photograph where one figure has become a flat grey rectangle. Elias's reflection sits in the glass.
characters: Elias Voss - reflection only, out of focus
scenes.environment: Desk by a window, framed photo, half-finished crossword, pencil shavings
scenes.lighting: Overcast window light, no fill; the grey rectangle reads as absence
scenes.camera: Static macro, rack focus from crossword to photograph
scenes.image_prompt: Vertical 9:16 macro still, a half-finished crossword with three answers erased into grey blocks, a framed family photograph beside it where one figure is a flat grey rectangle, overcast window light, dust, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine 16mm grain, melancholic, no readable words

scenes.narration: Saturday's paper arrived blank. Only the masthead remained. The Midnight Archive: all the news that never was.
scenes.visual: A blank broadsheet under a desk lamp. The masthead is the only ink on the page. The paper's whiteness is slightly too bright, as if lit from inside.
scenes.environment: Kitchen table, the same as scene 2, now cleared except for one sheet
scenes.lighting: Bare bulb directly above; the blank page reflects more light than it should
scenes.camera: Slow push in on the masthead, 50mm
scenes.image_prompt: Vertical 9:16 still, a completely blank broadsheet on a kitchen table under a bare bulb, only a small masthead printed at the top, paper glowing faintly white, hard shadows, teal-black room, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field, fine 16mm grain, uncanny stillness, minimal text

scenes.narration: Elias finally understood. It wasn't predicting his future. It was deciding what to keep.
scenes.visual: Elias sits in the dark, paper in his lap. He looks up at something just off camera. The lamp dies. One beat of black before the end card.
characters: Elias Voss - 34, face half-lit, no expression left to read
scenes.environment: His apartment, everything pushed to the walls, one chair in the middle
scenes.lighting: Half-face key light, then total darkness on the final word
scenes.camera: Very slow push in on the face; hard cut to black
